title: PII Handling & Log Redaction Request Flow — Prioritization Heuristics & Owner Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Define an operational triage flow and prioritization heuristics for customer requests related to PII handling, log redaction, retention windows, and audit export formats. Scope: non-bug customer requests (feature/configuration/legal requests) that require product, security, or infra action — e.g., redact user identifiers from request logs, reduce retention on per-customer basis, create an S3-formatted audit export with PII masking. Out of scope: incident response, real-time breach investigations, and billing disputes. Goals: 1) Create a repeatable routing matrix that maps request attributes to owners (Support, Security, PM, Dedicated Ops), 2) Define SLA tiers (Response, Assessment, Delivery) for Low/Medium/High business impact, 3) Produce decision rules (redact vs. shorten retention vs. pseudonymize vs. export) with trade-offs and required infra changes, 4) Deliver onboarding checklist and template responses for Support/SEs. Success metrics: median time-to-assess <= 3 business days for High, time-to-deliver for Low <= 30 days, % of requests auto-routed correctly >= 90% after rollout, post-delivery regressions <= 2 per quarter. Key decision heuristics: - Sensitive PII present in raw logs (SSN, full credit card numbers, raw biometric data) -> Escalate to Security + Dedicated Ops (High) and require redaction + audit export capability. - Identifiable user metadata (email, username) -> Preferred action: per-customer configurable retention or pseudonymization depending on contract terms. - Request for audit exports (legal/regulatory) -> translate to export format and retention policy; if PII required in export, require DPA review and KMS/HSM key access. Trade-offs to call out: aggressive redaction reduces observability and debuggability (increase MTTI), longer retention reduces cost but increases compliance burden. Roadmap & owners: 1) Triage matrix draft (PM owning) -> 2026-02-22, 2) Security policy and acceptance criteria (Security lead) -> 2026-03-01, 3) Small infra changes for per-customer retention + redaction toggle (ENG) -> spike in Cycle 11, 4) Templates & Support training (Customer Ops) -> pre-rollout. Instrumentation: track request type tags, owner routing, SLA timers, final disposition (redacted/retained/exported), and customer satisfaction. Deliverables: triage matrix doc, routing rules config (Support/Slack triage playbook), example redaction SDK patterns, Confluence runbook for Audit Exports. Acceptance criteria below. Risks & mitigations: - Misclassification of PII -> implement mandatory security review for any request flagged by Support as containing PII. - Infra complexity -> phase feature-gates and allow manual fallback. Open questions: 1) Per-customer retention UX surface (Console vs. API)? 2) Legal sign-off gating for exports containing PII? 3) Will Dedicated customers require different default SLAs? Next steps: align with Security on decision taxonomy, schedule 30-minute sync with Support and SEs, draft Confluence playbook for review.
acceptance_criteria: Triage matrix published in Confluence with mapping to owners and SLA tiers
Support and SEs have template responses and decision checklist
Automated routing rules created in Zendesk/Support for top-3 request types
Security sign-off documented for PII redaction and export flows
Instrumentation captures routing accuracy and SLA timers (dashboard visible)
